1281-tom-swift-and-his-aerial-warship-or.title: The Naval Terror of the Seas
1281-tom-swift-and-his-aerial-warship-or.creator: Unknown
1281-tom-swift-and-his-aerial-warship-or.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Here I go and get a half-holiday off from the bank, and just at the busiest time, too, to come and see you, and I find you in a brown study, looking as blue as indigo, and maybe you're all yellow inside from a bilious attack, for all I know."

arxiv-1708-04509.title: The Capacity of Some Classes of Polyhedra
arxiv-1708-04509.creator: Mojtaba Mohareri, Behrooz Mashayekhy, Hanieh Mirebrahimi
arxiv-1708-04509.description: Abstract K. Borsuk in 1979, in the Topological Conference in Moscow, introduced the concept of the capacity of a compactum. In this paper, we compute the capacity of the product of two spheres of the same or different dimensions and the capacity of lense spaces.

arxiv-1805-08701.title: Normalization of Transliterated Words in Code-Mixed Data Using Seq2Seq Model & Levenshtein Distance
arxiv-1805-08701.creator: Soumil Mandal, Karthick Nanmaran
arxiv-1805-08701.description: Abstract Building tools for code-mixed data is rapidly gaining popularity in the NLP research community as such data is exponentially rising on social media. Working with code-mixed data contains several challenges, especially due to grammatical inconsistencies and spelling variations in addition to all the previous known challenges for social media scenarios.

arxiv-2105-12746.title: Sculpting the sub-Saturn Occurrence Rate via Atmospheric Mass Loss
arxiv-2105-12746.creator: Tim Hallatt, Eve J. Lee
arxiv-2105-12746.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Tim Hallatt, Eve J. Lee. The sub-Saturn ( ∼ \sim 4–8 R ⊕ R_{\oplus} ) occurrence rate rises with orbital period out to at least ∼ \sim 300 days. In this work we adopt and test the hypothesis that the decrease in their occurrence towards the star is a result of atmospheric mass loss, which can transform sub-Saturns into sub-Neptunes ( ≲ \lesssim 4 R ⊕ R_{\oplus} ) more efficiently at shorter periods.

arxiv-2203-10015.title: Second-order optimality conditions for general nonconvex optimization problems and variational analysis of disjunctive systems
arxiv-2203-10015.creator: Matúš Benko, Helmut Gfrerer, Jane J. Ye, Jin Zhang, Jinchuan Zhou
arxiv-2203-10015.description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper, we propose second-order sufficient optimality conditions for a very general nonconvex constrained optimization problem, which covers many prominent mathematical programs. Unlike the existing results in the literature, our conditions prove to be sufficient, for an essential local minimizer of second order, under merely basic smoothness and closedness assumptions on the data defining the problem.

arxiv-2208-13695.title: A Data-Centric Approach For Dual-Arm Robotic Garment Flattening
arxiv-2208-13695.creator: Li Duan, Gerardo Aragon-Camarasa
arxiv-2208-13695.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Li Duan, Gerardo Aragon-Camarasa. Due to the high dimensionality of object states, a garment flattening pipeline requires recognising the configurations of garments for a robot to produce/select manipulation plans to flatten garments. In this paper, we propose a data-centric approach to identify known configurations of garments based on a known configuration network (KCNet) trained on depth images that capture the known configurations of garments and prior knowledge of garment shapes.

arxiv-2209-05936.title: How the non-metricity of the connection arises naturally in the classical theory of gravity Email: kijowski@cft.edu.pl
arxiv-2209-05936.creator: Bartłomiej Bąk
arxiv-2209-05936.description: Abstract Spacetime geometry is described by two – a priori independent – geometric structures: the symmetric connection Γ \Gamma and the metric tensor g g . Metricity condition of Γ \Gamma (i.e. ∇ g = 0 \nabla g=0 ) is implied by the Palatini variational principle, but only when the matter fields belong to an exceptional class.

arxiv-2303-05610.title: Perfectoid covers of abelian varieties and the weight-monodromy conjecture
arxiv-2303-05610.creator: Peter Wear
arxiv-2303-05610.description: Abstract . Deligne’s weight-monodromy conjecture gives control over the poles of local factors of L L -functions of varieties at places of bad reduction. His proof in characteristic p p was a step in his proof of the generalized Weil conjectures.

arxiv-2404-15134.title: Giant Spin-Orbit Torque in Cr-based Janus Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
arxiv-2404-15134.creator: Libor Vojáček, Joaquín Medina Dueñas, Jing Li, Fatima Ibrahim, Aurélien Manchon, Stephan Roche, Mairbek Chshiev, José H. García
arxiv-2404-15134.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Libor Vojáček, Joaquín Medina Dueñas, Jing Li, Fatima Ibrahim, Aurélien Manchon, Stephan Roche, Mairbek Chshiev, José H. García. We report a very large spin-orbit torque (SOT) capability of chromium-based transition metal dichalcogenides (TMD) in their Janus forms CrXTe, with X=S,Se.

arxiv-2404-18403.title: The defect b b -theorem under bulk RG flows
arxiv-2404-18403.creator: Tom Shachar a, Ritam Sinha b , and, Michael Smolkin a
arxiv-2404-18403.description: Abstract It is known that for RG flows confined to a two-dimensional defect, where the bulk maintains its conformal nature, the coefficient of the Euler density in the defect’s Weyl anomaly (termed b b ) cannot increase as the flow progresses from the ultraviolet to the infrared, a principle known as the b b -theorem.

arxiv-2406-15882.title: Equivalence Hypergraphs: DPO Rewriting for Monoidal E-Graphs
arxiv-2406-15882.creator: Aleksei Tiurin, Chris Barrett, Dan R. Ghica, Nick Hu
arxiv-2406-15882.description: Abstract The technique of equality saturation , which equips graphs with an equivalence relation, has proven effective for program optimisation. We give a categorical semantics to these structures, called e-graphs , in terms of Cartesian categories enriched over the category of semilattices.

arxiv-2410-07761.title: Jump Your Steps : Optimizing Sampling Schedule of Discrete Diffusion Models
arxiv-2410-07761.creator: Yonghyun Park & Chieh-Hsin Lai, Satoshi Hayakawa, Yuhta Takida, Yuki Mitsufuji
arxiv-2410-07761.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yonghyun Park & Chieh-Hsin Lai, Satoshi Hayakawa, Yuhta Takida, Yuki Mitsufuji. Diffusion models have seen notable success in continuous domains, leading to the development of discrete diffusion models (DDMs) for discrete variables. Despite recent advances, DDMs face the challenge of slow sampling speeds. While parallel sampling methods like τ \tau -leaping accelerate this process, they introduce Compounding Decoding Error (CDE), where discrepancies arise between the true distribution and the approximation from parallel token generation, leading to degraded sample quality.

arxiv-2506-04852.title: Improving AI-generated music with user-guided training
arxiv-2506-04852.creator: Vishwa Mohan Singh, Sai Anirudh Aryasomayajula, Ahan Chatterjee, Beste Aydemir, Rifat Mehreen Amin
arxiv-2506-04852.description: Abstract AI music generation has advanced rapidly, with models like diffusion and autoregressive algorithms enabling high-fidelity outputs. These tools can alter styles, mix instruments, or isolate them. Since sound can be visualized as spectrograms, image-generation algorithms can be applied to generate novel music.

arxiv-2507-10966.title: Evaluating the Predictive Power of Qualifying Performance in Formula One Grand Prix
arxiv-2507-10966.creator: Joshua Weissbock, Dr. Shirley Mills
arxiv-2507-10966.description: Abstract Formula One race weekends are structured around multiple sessions: practices, qualifying, and the Grand Prix itself, each contributing to final race performance. This study analyzes nearly two decades of races, encompassing 7,800 driver-weekend observations, to quantify the predictive value of each session on race outcomes.

arxiv-2512-07919.title: Quantum algorithms for viscosity solutions to nonlinear Hamilton-Jacobi equations based on an entropy penalisation method
arxiv-2512-07919.creator: Shi Jin, Nana Liu
arxiv-2512-07919.description: Abstract We present a framework for efficient extraction of the viscosity solutions of nonlinear Hamilton–Jacobi equations with convex Hamiltonians. These viscosity solutions play a central role in areas such as front propagation, mean-field games, optimal control, machine learning, and a direct application to the forced Burgers’ equation.

arxiv-2601-15955.title: JWST Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES) Data Release 5: MIRI Coordinated Parallels in GOODS-S and GOODS-N Facilities: JWST, HST JWST Calibration Pipeline, astropy, photutils, sep

Johnson, Jianwei Lyu (吕建伟), Jane Morrison, Pablo G. Pérez-González, George H. Rieke, Marcia Rieke, Pierluigi Rinaldi, Brant Robertson, Yang Sun,
arxiv-2601-15955.description: Abstract Medium to ultra-deep mid-infrared imaging surveys with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)’s Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) are reframing our view of the early Universe, from the emergence of ultra-red dusty and quiescent galaxies to the epoch of reionization to the first galaxies.

arxiv-2601-23059.title: On the Impact of Code Comments for Automated Bug-Fixing: An Empirical Study CCS: Software and its engineering Software development methods CCS: Software and its engineering Empirical software validation CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning
arxiv-2601-23059.creator: Antonio Vitale, Emanuela Guglielmi, Simone Scalabrino, Rocco Oliveto
arxiv-2601-23059.description: Abstract . Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly relevant in Software Engineering research and practice, with Automated Bug Fixing (ABF) being one of their key applications. ABF involves transforming a buggy method into its fixed equivalent. A common preprocessing step in ABF involves removing comments from code prior to training.

arxiv-2602-15123.creator: B. Bichang’a, D. De Cicco, S. Kaviraj, I. Lazar, A. Watkins, G. Martin, D. Kakkad

arxiv-2602-23324.title: Discrete turn strategies emerge in information-limited navigation
arxiv-2602-23324.creator: Jose M. Betancourt, Matthew P. Leighton, Thierry Emonet, Benjamin B. Machta, Michael C. Abbott
arxiv-2602-23324.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Jose M. Betancourt, Matthew P. Leighton, Thierry Emonet, Benjamin B. Machta, Michael C. Abbott. Navigation up a sensory gradient is one of the simplest behaviours, and the simplest strategy is run and tumble. But some organisms use other strategies, such as reversing direction or turning by some angle. Here we ask what drives the choice of strategy, which we frame as maximising up-gradient speed using a given amount of sensory information per unit time.

pmc-10537502.title: Successful Management, in a Low-Resource Setting, of Disseminated Tuberculosis in a 3-Year Old Boy: A Case Report
pmc-10537502.creator: Josina Chilundo, Arlindo Muhelo, Zita Ahivaldino, Helton Zucula, Sheila Macuácua, Ana Cristina Mussagi, Damiano Pizzol, Lee Smith, Giuseppe Maggioni
pmc-10537502.description: Disseminated or military tuberculosis (TB) is defined as the presence of at least two non-contiguous sites of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, occurring as a result of progressive primary infection, reactivation and spread of a latent focus or due to iatrogenic origin. Disseminated TB represents a life-threatening condition, especially in at-risk children and when diagnosis and treatment are delayed.

pmc-10545709.title: Early-melting snowpatch plant communities are transitioning into novel states
pmc-10545709.creator: John Morgan, Zac Walker
pmc-10545709.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Snowpatch plant community distribution and composition are strongly tied to the duration of long-lasting snow cover in alpine areas; they are vulnerable to global climatic changes that result in warmer temperatures and longer growing seasons. We used a revisitation study to quantify early-melting snowpatch floristic and functional diversity change in southern Australia, and document shrub size-class distributions over time to detect evidence for their encroachment into snowpatches, a key prediction with climatic change.

pmc-11513390.title: Multi-level barriers and facilitators to implementing evidence-based antipsychotics in the treatment of early-phase schizophrenia
pmc-11513390.creator: Allison J. Carroll, Delbert G. Robinson, John M. Kane, Avram Kordon, Jennifer Bannon, Theresa L. Walunas, C. Hendricks Brown
pmc-11513390.description: IntroductionLong-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotic medications and clozapine are effective yet underutilized medical therapies in early intervention services. The purpose of this study was to conduct a pre-implementation evaluation of contextual determinants of early intervention programs to implement innovations optimizing LAI antipsychotic and clozapine use within a shared decision-making model.

pmc-11518104.title: “We must make sacrifices” - coping among left-behind adolescents in Georgia after parental migration
pmc-11518104.creator: K Antia, V Winkler, A Berner Rodoreda
pmc-11518104.description: BackgroundAdolescence is challenging, particularly for those left-behind in their countries of origin while parents out-migrate for work. The Eastern European country Georgia has one of the highest percentages of left-behind children and adolescents worldwide, yet how they cope with migratory separation remains unknown. This study is the first to explore strategies of Georgian left-behind adolescents to cope with parental absence.

pmc-11672255.title: Impact of Viruses on Prokaryotic Communities and Greenhouse Gas Emissions in Agricultural Soils
pmc-11672255.creator: Xing Huang, Lucas P P Braga, Chenxiao Ding, Bokai Yang, Tida Ge, Hongjie Di, Yan He, Jianming Xu, Laurent Philippot, Yong Li
pmc-11672255.description: Viruses are abundant and ubiquitous in soil, but their importance in modulating greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in terrestrial ecosystems remains largely unknown. Here, various loads of viral communities are introduced into paddy soils with different fertilization histories via a reciprocal transplant approach to study the role of viruses in regulating greenhouse gas emissions and prokaryotic communities.

pmc-12698887.title: Fibroblast Growth Factor 8 Suppresses Neurotoxic Astrocytes and Alleviates Neuropathic Pain via Spinal FGFR3 Signaling
pmc-12698887.creator: Huizhu Liu, Lanxing Yi, Guiling Li, Kangli Wang, Hongsheng Wang, Yuqiu Zhang, Benlong Liu
pmc-12698887.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Astrocytes in the spinal dorsal horn (SDH) exhibit diverse reactive phenotypes under neuropathic conditions, yet the mechanisms driving this diversity and its implications in chronic pain remain unclear. Here, we report that spared nerve injury (SNI) induces marked upregulation of both complement component 3 (C3⁺, A1-like) and S100 calcium-binding protein A10 (S100A10⁺, A2-like) astrocyte subpopulations in the SDH, with elevated microglial cytokines including interleukin-1α, tumor necrosis factor-α, and complement component 1q.

pmc-12748535.title: Awareness of obesity’s causes is not linked to less Weight-Related bias
pmc-12748535.creator: Albert Lecube, Rodolfo J Galindo, Blanca Salinas-Roca, Iñaki Marina, Andreea Ciudin, Ana Belén Crujeiras, Cristóbal Morales, Sharona Azriel, Rafael Gómez-Blasco, César Bustos, Javier Butragueño, Lilliam Flores, Guillermo E Umpierrez, María M Malagón
pmc-12748535.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Weight stigma remains a major public health issue that negatively impacts individuals living with obesity. This study explores its prevalence in the Spanish adult population and examines whether viewing obesity as a disease influences societal attitudes. A representative sample of 1,000 adults participated in a Computer-Assisted Telephone Interview assessing knowledge, stereotypes, prejudice, and discrimination related to obesity, along with sociodemographic data and personal beliefs about its causes. While 40.8% attributed obesity to a lack of self-control, 59.2% considered it a disease.

pmc-12799854.title: Including people with lived experience in the development of the self-Dehumanisation in Psychosis Scale (DiPS): a reflective account
pmc-12799854.creator: Tom A. Jenkins, Anneli Bale, Linda Alush, Ed Brooks, Ian Carter, Eva Roberts, Pamela Jacobsen, Paul Chadwick
pmc-12799854.description: BackgroundLived experience involvement in measure development is recognised as best practice. This article is a reflective account, co-written between researchers and PPIE (Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement) consultants with lived experience of psychosis, about the impact of lived experience involvement in developing the self-Dehumanisation in Psychosis Scale (DiPS).

pmc-13210297.title: Exposure to Microplastics in Biological Matrices and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes in Children: A Systematic Review
pmc-13210297.creator: Francesco Fabrizio Comisi, Andrea Maria Comisi, Elena Esposito, Vassilios Fanos
pmc-13210297.description: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are ubiquitous environmental contaminants detected in numerous human tissues, yet epidemiological evidence on MNPs exposure and neurodevelopmental outcomes in children has not been systematically evaluated. We aimed to systematically identify, appraise, and synthesize observational evidence on this association in children aged 0–18 years.

pmc-13275331.title: Cognitive reserve against vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia: A scoping review
pmc-13275331.creator: Christopher E. Bauer, Colleen Pappas, Brian T. Gold
pmc-13275331.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID) are common in older adults and are typically associated with cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD). However, little remains known about non‐pharmacological, modifiable lifestyle variables that may build cognitive reserve against cSVD/VCID. To address this gap, we conducted a scoping review of the existing literature on this topic, following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. We identified and reviewed over 1000 articles that included keywords associated with cSVD/VCID and cognitive reserve.

pmc-13478631.title: Past projections of submediterranean oaks unveil future range shifts of vulnerable taxa under climate change
pmc-13478631.creator: Carlos Vila-Viçosa, Salvador Arenas-Castro, Antoine Guisan, Elif Deniz Ülker, Jean Stephan, Isabel Passos, Francisco M. Vázquez, Rubim Almeida, João Honrado, Cristina García, João Gonçalves
pmc-13478631.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Submediterranean marcescent oak forests form a climatic ecotone highly exposed to increasing aridity across the Mediterranean Basin. Understanding how these vulnerable taxa were affected by past climatic shifts can help contextualize their sensitivity to ongoing changes. Here we used ensemble Species Distribution Models (SDMs) to infer the distribution dynamics of eight marcescent oak species from the Heinrich Stadial (~ 17 ka) to the present, and to explore their potential future trajectories for 2070 and 2100 under three SSP scenarios.

pmc-13511475.creator: Hafize Nalan Güneş, Burcu Gökçe Çokal, Melih Altıkardeş, Gözde Orman, Sevim Kuyumcu, Gürsel Güneş, Levent Ertuğrul İnan

pmc-13534513.title: 3~14岁儿童屈光性散光和角膜散光患病率分析
pmc-13534513.creator: 雨暄 赵, 必 杨, 茴 罗, 蓉 李, 瑞 陈, 陇黔 刘, 乃红 闫
pmc-13534513.description: 目的调查四川省成都市3~14岁儿童屈光性散光（refractive astigmatism, RA）和角膜散光（corneal astigmatism, CA）患病率。方法采用随机抽样方法，纳入2024年成都市3个行政区内共500所学校（幼儿园、小学、中学）的学龄儿童散光筛查结果，收集患者基本信息以及非睫状肌麻痹下自动验光仪和眼光学生物测量仪测量的眼部参数信息。仅纳入患者右眼数据进行分析，比较不同年龄段儿童散光均值和散光发生率差异。 结果研究共纳入255 959名成都市3~14岁学龄儿童散光筛查结果，其中RA平均为（－0.56±0.59） D，CA平均为（－1.23±0.62） D，散光类型以顺规散光为主。RA（≤－1.00 D）和CA（≤－1.00 D）患病率分别为18.16%和62.29%。随年龄增长，散光屈光度和患病率呈现不同变化趋势（P<0.001），在3~8岁表现为RA和CA屈光度和患病率随年龄增加逐渐下降或保持稳定，在9~14岁表现为随年龄增加而不断增加。结论成都市3~14岁学龄儿童RA和CA屈光度以及患病率随年龄变化呈先下降或保持稳定后上升的趋势，中小学阶段散光患病率更高。 散光是常见的屈光不正之一，常和近视或远视同时发生[1]。散光的发生是由于眼屈光系统中，不同子午线的屈光力不同，从而导致视网膜成像不能形成一个焦点[2]。有研究显示，大多数儿童出生时即有一定散光，在婴儿和儿童期会出现下降，在青春期时会增加，在成年之后则会趋于稳定[3-4]。未矫正的轻度散光可能会影响视力，而未矫正的高度散光则可能影响儿童视觉发育，导致立体视丧失、对比敏感度下降、弱视等[5–7]。因此，早期筛查并矫正散光有利于儿童青少年的视觉发育。 目前，对散光成分研究较多的包括屈光性散光（refractive astigmatism, RA）和角膜散光（corneal astigmatism, CA）。RA即整个屈光系统的散光屈光度，屈光检查处方中常以负柱镜形式表示；CA是屈光性散光的一部分，通过角膜前表面等效折射率计算而得到，常使用角膜前表面最平坦子午线曲率与最陡峭子午线曲率之差计算。散光患病率因调查地区、种族、定义等因素而产生差异。许多研究对不同地区和年龄段儿童RA和CA患病率进行了调查，西安市一项横断面研究发现，2023年中小学整体RA患病率（≤－0.50 D）为59.3%，城市地区高于城乡结合地区[8]。Zhang等[9]在2020年对上海市学龄儿童调查显示，幼儿园RA和CA的患病率（≤－1.00 D）分别为15.8%和64.0%，在小学时期为16.5%和65.0%，而在高中时期增加至32.8%和76.9%。 近年来，大量研究聚焦于近视的发生发展，少部分研究对散光患病率及其影响因素进行分析。然而，散光同样影响着儿童视力，和近视一样，散光同样受遗传和环境因素的共同影响[1,10]。遗传因素中，父母散光程度、种族、性别、虹膜颜色等可能影响散光[10-11]，环境因素包括近距离用眼时间、户外活动时间等[1,9]。 前期已有一些研究对西安、上海等地散光患病率进行了调查，然而目前还没有针对四川省学龄儿童散光患病率的研究。因此本研究以学校为基础，纳入四川省成都市武侯区、高新区和郫都区三个区内的幼儿园和中小学散光筛查结果，调查不同年龄段儿童散光屈光度、类型以及患病率差异，从而为散光相关研究提供更多的循证依据。 资料与方法 研究对象 本研究是一项以学校为基础的横断面研究，纳入2024年四川省成都市学龄儿童散光筛查结果，采用系统自动生成的随机抽样方法，对武侯区、高新区和郫都区500所学校，不同年级和班级儿童进行抽查。本研究已获得四川大学华西医院伦理委员会批准，批准号2025年审（1290）号。研究主要针对成都市幼儿园、小学和中学三个阶段，因此纳入了有完整检查记录的3~14岁儿童青少年数据进行最终分析，排除以下可能影响散光或角膜形态的情况：1）有眼部手术史；2）有角膜接触镜配戴史；3）眼表瘢痕性疾病或任何导致角膜规则性受损的情况；4）眼部外伤（包括角膜、虹膜、晶状体等眼前节组织损伤）；5）先天性或遗传性眼病；6）其他影响屈光测量准确性的眼部疾病（如视网膜疾病、晶状体浑浊等）；7）疑似圆锥角膜或角膜扩张性疾病者。其中，对于筛查中发现角膜散光绝对值>3.00 D且矫正视力显著低于同年龄段正常范围的高度疑似圆锥角膜儿童，筛查团队将对其家长或监护人进行告知，并建议其至专业医疗机构进一步检查和确诊。由于本研究基于学校群体筛查，未对圆锥角膜患者进行深入统计分析，但已在数据清理阶段将其从分析样本中排除。 一般资料 研究收集了2024年四川省成都市高新区、武侯区和郫都区500所幼儿园及中小学共291 662名学龄儿童眼部健康检查数据，经纳排标准筛选后，排除了35 703名儿童数据，其中1127名儿童数据信息不完整，33 833名儿童年龄超过范围，9名儿童患有其他疾病，734名儿童使用过角膜接触镜。最终将255 959名儿童数据纳入最终分析，研究流程图如图1所示。受试者平均年龄为（8.64±3.05）岁，包括132 899名（51.92%）男性和123 060名（48.08%）女性。 Flow diagram of the subject enrollment process 研究筛选流程图 检查内容 研究期间所有眼科检查由研究团队中3位经验丰富的视光师完成，检查时间为2024年的春季和秋季学期。检查使用自动验光仪（RM800, 拓普康有限公司，日本）测量非睫状肌麻痹下的屈光度，使用眼光学生物测量仪（AL-Scan, 尼德克株式会社，日本）测量角膜曲率及眼轴长度。以问卷形式由被检查者监护人完成基本信息收集，包括年龄、性别、是否使用过角膜接触镜等，并告知监护人检查的目的和用途。 散光定义及标准 在本研究中，RA定义为自动验光仪负柱镜屈光度，轴向为负柱镜轴向；CA定义为眼光学生物测量仪测量结果中，角膜前表面最平坦子午线曲率与最陡峭子午线曲率之差，柱镜轴向为平坦子午线轴向。在计算散光患病率时，参考Zhang等[9]的研究，将发生RA与CA分别定义为RA≤－1.00 D和CA≤－1.00 D。散光类型分类参考Liang等[12]的研究，顺规散光（with the rule, WTR）定义为散光轴向≥0°且≤30°或散光轴向≥150°且≤180°；逆规散光（against the rule, ATR）定义为散光轴向≥60°且≤120°；斜轴散光（oblique, OBL）定义为散光轴向≥31°且≤59°或散光轴向≥121°且≤149°。 统计学方法 使用SPSS 29.

pmc-13684498.title: N 6 -methyladenosine regulates Influenza A virus mRNA stability yet is rarely found on genomic RNA
pmc-13684498.creator: Hsiu-Yi Wu, Wan-Ju Tung, Ramreishang Wungmaiwo, Pei-Yi (Alma) Su, Hung-Wei Hsu, Ankit Gupta, Brian N Papas, Marcos Morgan, Wen-Chun Liu, I-Hsuan Wang, Kevin Tsai
pmc-13684498.description: Previous studies have found widespread N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A methylation) on all forms of Influenza A virus (IAV) RNA, with m 6 A found critical for viral replication, pathogenicity as well as viral RNA packaging. Here we applied the latest quantitative technologies to revisit the methylation landscape on the anti-sense genomic RNA of IAV.
